stem.text: A file downloads at a rate of D(t) megabytes per second, where D is differentiable and t is measured in seconds. Measured values are D(0) = 20, D(2) = 24, D(3) = 30, D(8) = 14. Find the approximation to \( \int_{0}^{8} D(t)\,dt \), the number of megabytes downloaded from t = 0 to t = 8, given by a trapezoidal sum with the three subintervals indicated by these values. Give the exact value.

worked_solution.text: Each subinterval contributes its width times the average of its two endpoint values: \( 2 \cdot \frac{20 + 24}{2} = 44 \); \( 1 \cdot \frac{24 + 30}{2} = 27 \); \( 5 \cdot \frac{30 + 14}{2} = 110 \).

distractor_derivations.A: trapezoidal sum with the common width (b - a)/3 used for every subinterval
distractor_derivations.B: factor 1/2 applied to the first trapezoid only
distractor_derivations.C: left Riemann sum used in place of the trapezoidal sum
